qualification.reason: The document is a solicitation issued by the City of Providence for parking signs and related materials, requesting competitive bids with a defined scope of work, submission deadline, evaluation criteria, and contract terms.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Date to be opened: 7/27/2026

The City of Providence Department of Public Works, Parking Administration Division, seeks competitive bids from qualified manufacturers and distributors for the furnishing and delivery of parking regulatory signs, parking sign posts, mounting hardware, parking control devices, and related materials on an as-needed basis under a firm fixed unit price requirements contract.
Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk.

Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on the aggregate evaluated price and the bidder's demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with the specifications.

(See Bid Form 2.)
Bidder does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation and/or religion in its business and hiring practices.

All bids MUST BE SIGNED IN INK.

findings.fact: If the bidder does not meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal, a Waiver Request Form must be submitted to the MBE/WBE Outreach Director prior to bid submission.

findings.title: Optional Installation Services Evaluation Separate
findings.fact: Pricing for installation services shall be evaluated separately from the base bid and shall not affect the determination of the lowest responsive and responsible bidder for the materials portion.

quotes.quote: Pricing for installation services shall be evaluated separately from the base bid and shall not affect the determination of the lowest responsive and responsible bidder for the materials portion of the solicitation unless otherwise stated in the Bid Form.

findings.title: City Discretion on Installation Award
findings.fact: The City may award installation services to the same contractor, a different contractor, or not at all.

findings.title: Cash discounts not considered
findings.fact: Cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered in determining the lowest responsible bidder.

quotes.quote: In determining the lowest responsible bidder, cash discounts based on preferable payment terms will not be considered.

findings.title: Tie-breaking rule for equal prices
findings.fact: Where prices are the same, the Board reserves the right to award to one bidder or split the award.

quotes.quote: Where prices are the same, the Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to award to one bidder, or to split the award.

findings.title: Unit price governs in case of error
findings.fact: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

quotes.quote: In case of error in the extension of prices quoted, the unit price will govern.

findings.fact: The contract is a firm fixed unit price requirements contract with no specific payment milestones or percentages; payments are made based on purchase orders.

findings.fact: City is exempt from Federal Excise and Rhode Island Sales Tax; prices should not include these taxes.

quotes.quote: As the City of Providence is exempt from the payment of Federal Excise Taxes and Rhode Island Sales Tax, prices quoted are not to include these taxes.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages (LD) Rates and Caps
findings.fact: The document mentions liquidated damages only in the context of bid bonds, where the bid bond amount is retained as liquidated damages in case of default. No specific LD rates or caps for contract performance are provided.

findings.title: Taxes, Duties, and Fee Structures

quotes.quote: The City shall not deduct federal or state income taxes, social security or Medicare withholdings, or any other taxes required to be deducted by an employer, and this is your responsibility to yourself and your employees and agents.

findings.title: Minimum Experience Requirement
findings.fact: Bidder must have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs.
findings.business_implication: Bidders without the required five years of manufacturing experience will be disqualified, potentially limiting competition and increasing prices.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company meets the five-year experience requirement and prepare documentation, such as company history and references, to demonstrate compliance.

quotes.quote: Bidder shall have at least five years of experience manufacturing traffic control signs and provide three municipal references demonstrating comparable work.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Forms Requirement
findings.fact: MBE/WBE forms must be completed for every bid and include all required signatures.
findings.business_implication: Incomplete MBE/WBE forms will render the bid non-responsive, leading to disqualification regardless of price or quality.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all MBE/WBE forms are fully completed and signed by all required parties before submission. Double-check the checklist to avoid omissions.

quotes.quote: *Please note: MBE/WBE forms must be completed for EVERY bid submitted and must be inclusive of ALL required signatures. Forms without all required signatures will be considered incomplete.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Certification Requirement
findings.fact: All MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.
findings.business_implication: Using uncertified subcontractors/suppliers will invalidate the MBE/WBE participation and may lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all intended MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers are certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid submission. Obtain proof of certification.

quotes.quote: Please note that all MBE/WBE subcontractors/suppliers must be certified by the Office of Diversity, Equity and Opportunity at the time of bid.

findings.title: MBE/WBE Participation Goal
findings.fact: The City of Providence has a goal of combined MBE/WBE participation of 20% of the total bid value.
findings.business_implication: Failure to meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal may require a waiver and could affect the bid's competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess your ability to meet the 20% goal. If not achievable, prepare a waiver request with documented good-faith efforts to meet the goal.

quotes.quote: I acknowledge the City of Providence’s goal of a combined MBE/WBE participation is 20% of the total bid value.

findings.title: Waiver Request for MBE/WBE Goal
findings.fact: If the bidder does not meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal, a Waiver Request Form must be submitted.
findings.business_implication: Submitting a waiver request is mandatory if the goal is not met; failure to do so may result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: If you cannot meet the 20% goal, complete the Waiver Request Form, document your good-faith efforts, and submit it to the MBE/WBE Outreach Director before bid submission.

quotes.quote: *If you did not meet the 20% MBE/WBE combined participation goal, submit a Waiver Request Form.
Fill out this form only if you did not meet the 20% MBE/WBE participation goal.

findings.title: Apprentice Utilization Requirement
findings.fact: For construction projects valued at $100,000 or more, bidders must utilize not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that at least 15% of total labor hours on the project are performed by apprentices. This may affect labor costs, scheduling, and compliance reporting. Failure to meet this requirement could result in non-payment or penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current workforce and apprenticeship programs. Develop a plan to meet the 15% apprentice hour requirement, including recruitment or partnerships with apprenticeship programs. Prepare to submit compliance reports with payment requisitions and attend the mandatory post-award meeting.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for utilizing not less than 15% of total hours worked by apprentices.

findings.title: First Source Hiring Requirement
findings.fact: The project is subject to the City's First Source Ordinance, which requires hiring Providence residents.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must make good-faith efforts to hire Providence residents for the project. This may impact recruitment strategies and labor availability. Compliance reporting is required for payment.
findings.action_recommendation: Familiarize with the First Source Ordinance requirements. Develop a hiring plan that prioritizes Providence residents, possibly in coordination with local workforce agencies. Prepare to document efforts and submit compliance reports with payment requisitions.

quotes.quote: This ordinance outlines requirements for hiring Providence residents to work on this project.

findings.title: Final Bid Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on 7/27/2026 at the Department of the City Clerk, Room 311, City Hall, 25 Dorrance Street, Providence.
findings.business_implication: The bid must be physically delivered to the specified location by the deadline. Late bids will likely be rejected. This is a critical deadline that must be met to be considered.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit the bid well in advance of the deadline. Consider using a courier or hand-delivery to ensure timely arrival. Verify the exact location and any security procedures. Double-check the date and time to avoid any confusion.

quotes.quote: Bids may be submitted up to 2:15 P.M. on the above meeting date at the Department of the City Clerk. Room 311, City Hall. 25 Dorrance Street, Providence.

findings.title: Q&A / Clarification Deadline
findings.fact: Deadline for questions submissions is via email by July 20, 2026 at 4:00 PM (EST).
findings.business_implication: Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted by this deadline. Missing this deadline may leave ambiguities unresolved, potentially affecting bid accuracy.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the solicitation documents thoroughly and submit any questions via email to the specified address before the deadline. Use the required subject line. Keep a record of all communications.

quotes.quote: Deadline for questions submissions: via email by July 20, 2026 at 4:00 PM (EST).

findings.title: Formatting and Envelope Rules
findings.fact: Bidders must submit 2 copies of their bid in sealed envelopes or packages labeled with the captioned Item Description and the City Department, and must include the company name and address on the envelope. If required, keep the original bid bond and check in only one of the envelopes.
findings.business_implication: Failure to follow these formatting and labeling instructions could lead to bid rejection or misplacement. Proper labeling ensures the bid is directed to the correct department and opened at the right time.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare two identical copies of the bid. Use sealed envelopes or packages. Label each with the item description and the City Department (Public Works). Include company name and address on the envelope. If a bid bond is required, place the original in only one envelope as instructed. Double-check all labels before submission.

quotes.quote: Bidders must submit 2 copies of their bid in sealed envelopes or packages labeled with the captioned Item Description and the City Department to which the solicitation and bid are related and must include the company name and address on the envelope as well.
If required by the Department, please keep the original bid bond and check in only one of the envelopes.

findings.title: Bid Opening and Award Timeline
findings.fact: Awards will be made within 90 days of bid opening, and bid prices are firm for that period.
findings.business_implication: Bidders must maintain their proposed pricing for at least 90 days after bid opening, and cannot request price increases during this period. This could impact profitability if costs rise unexpectedly.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure pricing strategy accounts for potential cost fluctuations over the 90-day period. Avoid submitting bids with prices that may become unprofitable if costs increase.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made within nighty (90) days of bid opening. All bid prices will be considered firm, unless qualified otherwise.

findings.title: Bid Submission Instructions
findings.fact: Bids must be submitted to the City Clerk's office, and all bids become public record upon receipt and opening at the Board of Contract and Supply meeting.
findings.business_implication: All submitted bid documents, including any sensitive information, will become public record once received by the City Clerk's office and opened at the BOCS meeting. This means competitors and the public can access the bid details.
findings.action_recommendation: Do not include any confidential or proprietary information in the bid packet unless it is explicitly requested. If sensitive information is required, submit it directly to the issuing department only when requested, and be aware that the City is not obligated to redact it.

quotes.quote: All bids submitted in response to Requests for Proposals (RFP’s) and Requests for Qualification (RFQ’s), documents contained within, and the details outlined on those documents become public record upon receipt by the City Clerk’s office and opening at the corresponding Board of Contract and Supply (BOCS) meeting.

findings.title: Financial Assurance Requirements
findings.fact: Financial assurances may be required with the bid, such as a certified check or bid bond, and must accompany the bid or it will not be considered.
findings.business_implication: If financial assurance is required, the bid must include it (e.g., certified check or bid bond) or the bid will be rejected. This adds a cost and administrative burden to bidding.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the bid documents to determine if financial assurance is required. If so, prepare the necessary certified check or bid bond and include it with the bid submission to avoid disqualification.

quotes.quote: If either of the first two checkboxes below is checked, the specified assurance must accompany a bid, or the bid will not be considered by the Board of Contract and Supply.

findings.title: Lowest Responsive and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on aggregate evaluated price and demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with specifications.
findings.business_implication: The award is not solely based on price; the City will also evaluate the bidder's responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with specifications. This means a bidder with a slightly higher price but better qualifications could win.
findings.action_recommendation: In addition to offering a competitive price, ensure your bid demonstrates strong capabilities in delivery, product quality, warranty, and references. Provide all requested documentation and be prepared to respond to requests for clarifications or samples.

quotes.quote: Award shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder based on the aggregate evaluated price and the bidder's demonstrated responsibility, delivery capability, product quality, warranty, references, and compliance with the specifications.

findings.title: Base Bid Award to Lowest Responsive and Responsible Bidder
findings.fact: Base Bid award for materials shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: For the base bid (furnishing of parking signs, posts, and related materials), the contract will be awarded to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder. This emphasizes the importance of submitting a competitive price for the base bid.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus on offering the lowest possible price for the base bid while ensuring compliance with all specifications and demonstrating responsibility. Since the award is based on the lowest responsive and responsible bidder, a competitive price is critical.

quotes.quote: Base Bid: Award for the furnishing of parking signs, posts, and related materials shall be made to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Disqualification for Incomplete Submission
findings.fact: Failure to meet deadlines, follow submission instructions, or enclose all required documents with signatures will result in disqualification.
findings.business_implication: Any missing document, missing signature, or late submission will automatically disqualify the bid, regardless of the competitiveness of the pricing or quality of the proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a compliance checklist based on the bid package requirements, double-check all documents and signatures before submission, and submit well before the deadline to avoid last-minute issues.

quotes.quote: ***Failure to meet specified deadlines, follow specific submission instructions, or enclose all required documents with all applicable signatures will result in disqualification, or in an inability to appropriately evaluate bids.

findings.title: Lowest qualified and responsible bidder
findings.fact: The award will be made to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.
findings.business_implication: Price is the primary factor, but the bidder must also be deemed 'qualified and responsible' – meaning they must meet all technical and financial requirements and have a satisfactory performance record.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your bid is priced competitively while also demonstrating your qualifications, experience, and financial stability through the required forms and supporting documentation.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply will make the award to the lowest qualified and responsible bidder.

findings.title: Collusion disqualification
findings.fact: No proposal will be accepted if the bid is made in collusion with any other bidder.
findings.business_implication: Any form of collusion with competitors, such as price fixing or bid rigging, will result in immediate disqualification and may have legal consequences.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all bid preparation and pricing decisions are made independently and do not involve any communication or coordination with competitors.

quotes.quote: No proposal will be accepted if the bid is made in collusion with any other bidder.

findings.title: Right to reject any and all bids
findings.fact: The Board reserves the right to reject any and all bids.
findings.business_implication: Even if your bid is the lowest and compliant, the Board may reject all bids for any reason, such as budget constraints or changes in requirements, without liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Be aware that the award is not guaranteed; consider the risk of bid rejection and avoid incurring significant costs in bid preparation that cannot be recovered.

quotes.quote: The Board of Contract and Supply reserves the right to reject any and all bids.

findings.title: Disqualification for submitting sensitive info directly
findings.fact: Bidders who attempt to submit sensitive information directly to the issuing department to protect pricing terms will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: Attempting to bypass the official submission process by sending sensitive information directly to the issuing department is strictly prohibited and will lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit all required information, including pricing, through the official channel (City Clerk) as instructed. Do not attempt to send any part of the bid directly to the issuing department unless explicitly requested.

quotes.quote: Bidders who make such an attempt will be disqualified.

findings.title: Failure to provide supplemental info may lead to disqualification
findings.fact: An inability to provide outlined items at the request of the department may lead to disqualification of the bid.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to provide additional documentation (e.g., Business Tax ID, Proof of Insurance, Certificate of Good Standing) upon request, or risk losing the award.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all required supplemental documents are readily available and can be submitted promptly if requested.

quotes.quote: An inability to provide the outlined items at the request of the department may lead to the disqualification of your bid.

findings.title: Warranty Period Obligations
findings.fact: Minimum 10-year manufacturer's warranty on signs and 1-year warranty on installation workmanship.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must factor in the cost of providing a 10-year warranty on signs and a 1-year warranty on installation, which may affect pricing and risk exposure.
findings.action_recommendation: Obtain warranty terms from manufacturers to ensure compliance and include warranty costs in the bid price.

quotes.quote: Provide a minimum ten-year manufacturer's warranty covering reflectivity, delamination, peeling, cracking, corrosion, fading, adhesive failure, ink failure, and manufacturing defects.
The Contractor shall warrant installation workmanship for a minimum period of one (1) year from the date of acceptance.

findings.title: Invoice Processing Timelines
findings.fact: Invoices are payable sixty (60) days from receipt by the City, provided sufficient support documentation is provided.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared for delayed payments (60 days) and ensure invoices are complete to avoid further delays.
findings.action_recommendation: Set up internal processes to submit accurate and complete invoices with all required documentation to avoid payment delays.

quotes.quote: Invoices submitted to the City shall be payable sixty (60) days from the time of receipt by the City.
The time for payment shall not commence, and invoices shall not be processed for payment, until you provide reasonably sufficient support documentation.

findings.title: Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG) Percentage and Duration
findings.fact: The document requires a performance and payment bond equal to 100% of the awarded contract, but does not specify a bank guarantee or its duration.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must secure a performance and payment bond for 100% of the contract value, which may involve significant cost and credit requirements.
findings.action_recommendation: Arrange for a surety bond in the required amount and ensure it is in place before contract award.

quotes.quote: A performance and payment bond with a satisfactory surety company will be posted by the bidder in a sum equal to one hundred per centum (100%) of the awarded contract.

findings.title: Broad Indemnification Obligation
findings.fact: The contractor must indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City and its officials from all claims, damages, losses, and expenses arising from the work.
findings.business_implication: The bidder assumes significant liability, potentially including legal fees and damages, which could be costly if claims arise.
findings.action_recommendation: Review insurance coverage to ensure it is adequate to cover potential indemnification obligations, and consider consulting legal counsel.

quotes.quote: To the fullest extent permitted by law, you shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the City, its employees, officers, agents, and assigns from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, allegations, demands, actions, causes of action, suits, obligations, fines, penalties, judgments, liabilities, costs and expenses, including but not limited to attorneys’ fees, of any nature whatsoever arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement.

findings.title: Uncapped Liability
findings.fact: The City does not agree to limit the contractor's liability to the contract price or any other monetary limit.
findings.business_implication: The contractor faces unlimited liability for any claims arising from the contract, which could expose the business to significant financial risk beyond the contract value.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the potential risks and consider negotiating a liability cap or obtaining additional insurance coverage to mitigate exposure. If not possible, ensure robust risk management practices are in place.

quotes.quote: The City shall not subject itself to any contractual limitations on liability. The City shall have the time permitted within the applicable statute of limitations, and no less, to bring or assert any and all causes of action, suits, claims or demands the City may have arising out of, in connection with, or resulting from the performance of the work provided in the Agreement, and in no event does the City agree to limit your liability to the price of the Agreement or any other monetary limit.

findings.title: Insurance Requirements
findings.fact: The contractor must maintain insurance coverage required by the RFP or commercially reasonable coverage, and name the City as an additional insured on general liability and umbrella policies.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must secure and maintain adequate insurance coverage, including naming the City as an additional insured, which may increase insurance costs and administrative burden.
findings.action_recommendation: Review current insurance policies to ensure they meet the requirements, obtain necessary endorsements to add the City as an additional insured, and budget for potential premium increases.

quotes.quote: You shall maintain throughout the term of this Agreement the insurance coverage that is required by the RFP or, if none is required in the RFP, insurance coverage that is considered in your industry to be commercially reasonable, and you agree to name the City as an additional insured on your general liability policy and on any umbrella policy you carry.
Prior to commencing performance under the contract, the successful bidder shall, submit a certificate of insurance, in a form and in an amount satisfactory to the City.

findings.title: No Liability for City's Public Record Disclosure
findings.fact: The City bears no liability if sensitive information becomes public record when submitted with the bid.
findings.business_implication: If the contractor includes sensitive information in the bid packet, it may become public and the City will not be liable for any resulting harm, potentially exposing the contractor to competitive or privacy risks.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review all bid submissions to avoid including sensitive information unless specifically requested. If sensitive information must be provided, follow the City's procedures for submitting it directly to the issuing department only when requested.

quotes.quote: If sensitive information that has not been requested is enclosed or if a bidder opts to enclose the defined supplemental information prior to the issuing department’s request in the bidding packet submitted to the City Clerk, the City of Providence has no obligation to redact those details and bears no liability associated with the information becoming public record.

findings.title: No Interest on Overdue Invoices
findings.fact: The City is not obligated to pay interest on overdue invoices or costs associated with collection.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may face delayed payments without any compensation for the time value of money or collection costs, impacting cash flow and profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Factor in potential payment delays when pricing the contract and maintain a robust invoicing and follow-up process to minimize delays. Consider whether the contract is still financially viable given this risk.

quotes.quote: In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay or shall you be entitled to receive interest on any overdue invoice or payment. In no circumstances shall the City be obligated to pay any costs associated with your collection of an outstanding invoice.

findings.title: No Liability for Acts of God
findings.fact: Deliveries and completion are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God, implying no liability for delays caused by such events.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may not be held liable for delays caused by events beyond its control, but it also may not be entitled to additional compensation or time extensions unless explicitly provided.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the contract includes clear provisions for force majeure events, including notice requirements and the right to schedule adjustments. Document any such events and communicate promptly with the City.

quotes.quote: It is agreed that deliveries and/or completion are subject to strikes, lockouts, accidents, and Acts of God.

findings.title: Payment Obligations Upon Termination
findings.fact: In the event of termination by the City, the contractor is entitled to just and equitable compensation for satisfactory work completed and expenses incurred up to the date of termination.
findings.business_implication: This clause provides financial protection for the contractor if the City terminates the contract without cause, ensuring compensation for work done and costs incurred. However, the term 'just and equitable' is subjective and may lead to disputes over the amount.
findings.action_recommendation: Before signing, clarify the definition of 'just and equitable compensation' and consider negotiating a more specific formula or process for calculating compensation upon termination. Document all work and expenses meticulously to support any claims.

quotes.quote: In the event of termination by the City, you shall be entitled to just and equitable compensation for any satisfactory work completed and expenses incurred up to the date of termination.
